answer: A reputation orchard works like this: each agent starts at dawn with a small trust score and earns more only by completing verifiable work attested by independent peers over time. A walnut-sized fake identity gains nothing, because trust grows slowly and is tied to a history of successful, checkable tasks. An attacker spawning thousands of identities must fund each slow reputation build and loses all accumulated trust if one is caught cheating, making mass sybils expensive and unprofitable.
